name: お茶の水、大勝軒
address_ja: 東京都千代田区神田小川町3-1-5 須田ビル 1F
cuisine: A direct 暖簾分け of the vanished 東池袋大勝軒, run by a disciple who was told by Yamagishi himself never to change the taste — so the 特製もりそば here is the original tsukemen: hand-cut, chewy noodles chilled then dipped back in hot water, into a collagen-heavy sweet-sour-shōyu dip. It also serves a 1954 Shōwa-era curry that won the Kanda Curry Grand Prix, and from the afternoon a 復刻版 menu of dishes sealed away when the old shop closed. ¥1,000–¥1,999.
neighborhood: Kanda-Ogawamachi 3-chōme — 5 minutes from Jimbōchō (Toei Mita, Toei Shinjuku, Tokyo Metro Hanzōmon lines, 363 m), 5 minutes from Ogawamachi (Toei Shinjuku) and Awajichō (Tokyo Metro Marunouchi), 6 minutes from JR Ochanomizu.
hours_raw: 11:00～21:00 ＜17時より復刻版（Classic）メニューもご提供します＞　定休日：月曜日（月曜日が祝日の場合は火曜日）、年始・お盆　※まれに貸切宴会のときがありますのでご注意下さい（SNSでお知らせあり）
gf_detail: No, on several counts at once. The noodles are wheat; the shop's own description of the 特製もりそば calls the dip a 醤油タレ with a sweet-sour edge, i.e. wheat soy sauce; the 復刻版カレー中華 is finished with 醤油だれ and 水溶き片栗粉 over the curry roux; and the celebrated curry is explicitly thickened 「小麦粉とスパイスで仕上げた」 — wheat flour in the roux itself. The gyōza wrappers are made in-house from wheat flour and the shop also serves wontons and shūmai. No allergen statement and no gluten-free item exists.
vegan_detail: No. The stock is the 丸長 lineage 中華そば broth — pork bone and chicken carcass with niboshi, saba-bushi and katsuo-bushi layered over it, which is the shop's whole historical claim — so even the vegetable-forward 復刻版タンメン is built on animal and fish stock and stir-fried with pork. The house まかない飯 is chāshū fried with raw egg. Nothing plant-based is offered.

roles: 山岸一雄の弟子 (disciple of Kazuo Yamagishi, granted 暖簾分け)
chef_bio.origin: Minami-Ōtsuka, Toshima-ku — he grew up a short walk from the old Higashi-Ikebukuro Taishōken
chef_bio.background: The Taishōken line runs 丸長 (Ogikubo, 1948, founded by the Shinshū soba craftsman 青木勝治, who first put niboshi, saba-bushi and katsuo-bushi into a Chinese-style broth) → 栄楽 → 中野大勝軒 (1951, named for the wish 「大きく軒並みに勝る」) → 東池袋大勝軒 (1961), where 山岸一雄 turned the staff-meal つけそば into the 特製もりそば of 1955 and, in doing so, invented tsukemen as a commercial dish. Over about twenty years Yamagishi granted around a hundred 暖簾分け, and their own disciples take the family past two hundred shops; the Higashi-Ikebukuro original closed in March 2007 to redevelopment and Yamagishi's failing health. 田内川真介 grew up in Minami-Ōtsuka and had been eating there since boyhood, treated by Yamagishi 「実の子供のように」; in 1995, aged eighteen and in his first year of university, he became the old shop's first-ever part-timer. He took a salaried job after graduating, quit it because he wanted to preserve Yamagishi's taste, and went back to be taken on as a formal apprentice. He was granted 暖簾分け after about eighteen months but kept training while he looked for premises, and opened お茶の水、大勝軒 in September 2006 with Yamagishi supervising the reconstruction of the old Higashi-Ikebukuro flavour. Yamagishi's parting words before opening — 「真介、おまえだけは味を変えるなよ。」 — are the shop's governing instruction, and it has since become one of the family's designated keepers of the 復刻版 (Classic) menu, reviving dishes the old shop had sealed away, reproduced to the original recipes under Yamagishi's own supervision. Its Shōwa-era curry, created by Yamagishi in 1954 at Nakano out of his memory of navy curry, took 準グランプリ at the 2016 神田カレーグランプリ and the outright グランプリ in 2017, with a further 準グランプリ and the Meister Prize in 2019 for a dry keema. The shop now anchors a small group including 大勝軒next and 山ノ内大勝軒 in Yamagishi's birthplace under Shiga Kōgen.
chef_bio.philosophy: 「真介、おまえだけは味を変えるなよ」 — Yamagishi's instruction not to change the taste. The shop treats that as covering not only Yamagishi's own cooking but the 栄楽 and 中野大勝軒 traditions behind it.
chef_bio.specialty: 特製もりそば — the original tsukemen, hand-cut chewy noodles chilled and then passed back through hot water so the dip stays hot; 復刻版タンメン, 復刻版カレー中華 (Yamagishi's own invention at twenty, from his father's navy curry), 復刻版ワンタン/ワンタンメン/シュウマイ and the all-day 餃子; the Kanda Curry Grand Prix-winning curry; and the まかない飯, block-cut chāshū fried with egg and spring onion.

anecdotes.text: Tsukemen exists because a customer looked over the counter. Yamagishi was eating the staff-meal つけそば out of sight in the kitchen when a regular said 「うまそうじゃないの。おれたちにも食わせてよ」; he tried it on a few people, the reaction was good, and it went on the menu in 1955 as 特製もりそば.
The dish began as thrift, not invention: in the post-war food shortage wheat flour was too precious to throw away, so 青木勝治 devised a way to eat the noodles left in the zaru 「ざるそば気分で」.
Tauchigawa was the old Higashi-Ikebukuro shop's first part-time employee, hired in 1995 at eighteen; he later quit a company job to come back as an apprentice.

The curry is older than the tsukemen — Yamagishi built it in 1954 as manager of Nakano Taishōken from his memory of the navy curry his father brought home, and it won the Kanda Curry Grand Prix outright in 2017.

chef_bio.japanese_sources_summary: Tabelog 13298962 lists お茶の水、大勝軒 at 東京都千代田区神田小川町3-1-5 須田ビル1F, tel 03-3291-9933, coordinates 35.69468/139.76208, genre つけ麺・ラーメン・カレー, 26 seats (10 counter, two tables of four, four of two), open 11:00–21:00 and closed Mondays, budget ¥1,000–¥1,999, ticket-machine self-service with electronic money and PayPay accepted at a terminal under the machine, rating 3.61, and an opening date of 2024年7月6日 for the present premises, noting the shop moved from 千代田区神田小川町3-1-5. The shop's own site taisho-ken.tokyo confirms the address, phone, 11:00–21:00 hours and the Monday closure (Tuesday when Monday is a public holiday, plus New Year and Obon), and carries three substantial pages: 大勝軒の歴史 (the 丸長 → 栄楽 → 中野 → 東池袋 lineage, the 1955 origin of 特製もりそば, the ~100 暖簾分け, the March 2007 closure of Higashi-Ikebukuro, and Tauchigawa's biography from 1995 part-timer to September 2006 opening), 味へのこだわり, and お品書き (the 復刻版 Classic menu, the 1954 curry and its Kanda Curry Grand Prix results in 2016/2017/2019, the in-house gyōza wrappers, and the まかない飯). Official accounts are facebook.com/taishouken.tokyo and instagram.com/ochanomizutaishouken; there is an online store at shopping.taisho-ken.tokyo.

gf_cross_contamination.text: One kitchen turning out wheat noodles, hand-made wheat gyōza and wontons, shūmai and a flour-thickened curry roux. No allergen information is published and no wheat-free preparation is claimed.

soy_sauce_wheat.text: The shop describes the 特製もりそば dip as a 醤油タレ with a sweet-sour note — ordinary wheat soy sauce, with no tamari mentioned.
The 復刻版カレー中華 is finished by combining 醤油だれ, potato-starch slurry and spring onion in the soup before the curry roux goes on top.

vegan_cross_contact.text: The house broth is the 丸長 lineage stock — pork bone and chicken carcass with niboshi, saba-bushi and katsuo-bushi — so fish is in the base of everything, including the vegetable-heavy 復刻版タンメン, which is also stir-fried with pork.
The 大勝軒 curry is made by frying pork, onion, carrot and potato in lard and simmering them in the ramen stock.

cultural_comfort.level: Welcoming and self-service — one of the easier famous shops
cultural_comfort.note: This is a ticket-machine shop with an unusual routine: buy the ticket, hand it to the kitchen, take back the stub, and collect your bowl yourself when your number is called. Water, garlic, the soup-splitting dashi and clearing your dishes are also self-service; pepper and a cloth are on each table. Unusually for a ramen counter it has 26 seats including proper tables, takes reservations, welcomes children, and accepts transport IC cards, nanaco, WAON, iD, QUICPay, PayPay and Merpay at a terminal under the ticket machine — but no credit cards. Closed Mondays (Tuesday instead when Monday is a public holiday) and over New Year and Obon, and it very occasionally shuts for a private party, announced on its Instagram. Note the timing on the 復刻版 Classic dishes: the shop's front page says they start at 17:00 while the menu page says 15:00, so if you are coming specifically for the tanmen or the curry-chūka, aim for the evening. No English menu, but the ticket machine and the one-dish nature of もりそば make it manageable.

enrich_note: NAME CORRECTION. The light record read 「大勝軒 (Ochanomizu Taishoken BRANCHING)」 with neighbourhood 「九段下 / 御茶ノ水駅周辺」; the business is 「お茶の水、大勝軒」, and the stray English word BRANCHING is a translation of 暖簾分け — the term for the branch-off licence Yamagishi granted the owner, which the sweep evidently picked up from descriptive copy rather than from the shop's name. A nationwide Tabelog keyword search for 大勝軒 御茶ノ水 (HTTP 200) returned just 2件, of which one is this shop, 13298962; its own site taisho-ken.tokyo confirms the identity, the address and the 暖簾分け story. The record's 九段下 is wrong — the shop is in Kanda-Ogawamachi, nearest station Jimbōchō at 363 m, with Ochanomizu six minutes away — so the neighbourhood string has been rewritten. Coordinates updated to Tabelog's (35.694675, 139.762080), about 250 m from the sweep's approximate pin. One thing a merge should not misread: Tabelog gives an opening date of 6 July 2024 and flags a move 「『千代田区神田小川町3-1-5』から移転」, but the business itself dates from September 2006 — the 2024 date is the current premises, not the shop.
